Karunanidhi, Hon'ble former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, during the Budget Speech 1997-98, announced the Namakku Naame Thittam (NNT) to encourage people's participation in the creation of public assets. The scheme aims to promote and strengthen the self-help and self-reliant attitude of the rural community. Individuals, groups, institutions, companies or the local community can choose work by accepting to contribute a minimum of one-third of the cost for the works under this scheme. In SC/ST habitations, the minimum public contribution should be 1/5 th of the estimated amount of the work. From the year 2021-22 this scheme is implemented in rural areas with an allocation of Rs.100 crore per year. During the year 2021-22, 2,148 works have been takenup at an estimate cost of Rs.156.71 crore including public contribution, 2,127 works have been completed and remaining 21 works are in progress. During the year 2022-23, 1,579 works have been takenup at an estimate cost of Rs.134.71 crore including public contribution, 1,449 works have been completed and remaining 130 works are in progress. For the year 2023-24 a sum of Rs.100 crore was released for implementation of the scheme. In addition to that based on the proposals received from the districts , a sum of Rs.50 crore is sanctioned as additional fund by the Government for the year 2023-24. During the year 2023-24 2,051 works have been takenup at an estimate cost of Rs.249.62 crore including public contribution, 664 works have been completed and remaining 1,387 works are in progress.
